fragments.derived_text: Write your character's level on your character sheet. Typically, a character starts at level 1 and advances in level by adventuring and gaining Experience Points (XP). Your GM might start you at a higher level.

Once you have generated six scores, assign them to Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. Determine ability modifiers using this table: score 3 gives -4; 4–5 gives -3; 6–7 gives -2; 8–9 gives -1; 10–11 gives +0; 12–13 gives +1; 14–15 gives +2; 16–17 gives +3; 18–19 gives +4; and 20 gives +5.
The Character Advancement table gives this Proficiency Bonus by character level: levels 1–4 +2; 5–8 +3; 9–12 +4; 13–16 +5; and 17–20 +6.

Your Proficiency Bonus is based on your total character level, not your level in a particular class. For example, a level 3 Fighter / level 2 Rogue has the Proficiency Bonus of a level 5 character, which is +3.
